title: From the Basement to the Bowl: Sonny's Ben Dover Goes Worst to First in Buckaroo Bowl III
dek: Two straight last places, then a 13-3 season and a title, while Kaushal's league-best points bought him only third and Mekhi's monster week couldn't keep the Dawgs out of the cellar.
body: For two years, the Buckaroo Football League had a reliable floor, and it was Sonny. Ben Dover finished last in 2023, last again in 2024, and posted the worst week of last season for good measure. So naturally, 2025 was the year the commissioner flipped the whole standings table over. Ben Dover went 13-3, took the No. 1 seed with 1,850.8 points, and won Buckaroo Bowl III. Worst to first is no longer a hopeful storyline. It's on the trophy.

The draft set up some trouble early, and Mekhi felt it first. Kai, who probably knows more football than anyone in the group, drafted from basic training, which is about the least ideal draft room in fantasy history. He clawed back anyway, playing the waiver wire like he owned it, and in week 9 the Dawgs dropped 153.62, the highest single-week score of the season. Remember that number, because the ending of his story does not match it.

The year's biggest plot twist happened off the field. Ramon ran Araleasers through week 8, and that stretch included the season's lowest score, a 61.4 in week 3. Then Brucie was kicked from the league for inactivity. The team became Ramon's Remains, played out the year on autopilot, and promptly won its first managerless game, 94.76 to 92.02 over Alan in week 9. Those results still count on Ramon's record with an asterisk attached, meaning Brucie now owns wins he wasn't even there for. Losing to a team with nobody steering it is a special kind of humbling, and Philly will be hearing about it.

The cruelest math belongs to Kaushal. Habibsters scored 1,973.6 points, the most in the league by more than 115, and went 8-8. Habib piled up points all fall and kept drawing opponents who picked his week to have their best one, which is a strange way to lose your grip on a two-year title. The 3 seed was the reward, and even that didn't last long.

The playoffs belonged to the two best records. Randy's The fumblers, 9-7 and the 2 seed, flattened Habibsters 137.1 to 79.96, a 57-point margin that ended Kaushal's reign without any drama at all. After finishing fourth in 2024 with the league's top offense, Randy finally got his points to show up in January and earned his first trip to a Buckaroo Bowl. Also new this year: the league made 4 trades after two seasons of zero, so a market finally exists, even if the jury is still out on how much Randy shopped in it.

Buckaroo Bowl III was a tight, grinding finish rather than a blowout. Ben Dover beat The fumblers 105.1 to 86.48, and the commissioner closed out the greatest single-season turnaround the BFL has ever seen. Sonny may live in Boston now, but this was pure Chicago: two years of misery followed by one glorious season nobody saw coming. Randy takes runner-up, which comes with more complaining rights than he had last year and exactly the same number of trophies.

The consolation ladder did the strangest work of all. Alan entered as the 6 seed at 5-11 and climbed to fourth, Ramon's Remains took fifth, and Mekhi's Dawgs, 8-8 with 1,858.2 points and the season's biggest week, fell all the way to last. Kai outscored the champion and still ended up in the basement Sonny just vacated. The league grows to eight teams in 2026, and the record book now reads: Buckaroo Bowl III, Ben Dover, champion; Dawgs, last place. Everyone else gets the offseason to figure out how the commish pulled it off.
